title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Determine the Time Limit for Raising Objections to the Inherent Quality of Industrial and Mineral Products Where There Is No Statutory or Contractual Time Limit

articles.content_en:
Supreme People's Court
Reply on How to Determine the Time Limit for Raising Objections to the Intrinsic Quality of Industrial and Mineral Products in the Absence of Statutory or Contractual Time Limits
Fa Jing [1993] No. 195
Higher People's Court of Shandong Province:
Your court's Request for Guidance on How to Determine the Time Limit for Raising Objections to the Intrinsic Quality of Products in the Absence of Statutory or Contractual Time Limits (Lu Gao Fa Han [1992] No. 218) has been received. After study, the reply is as follows:
In a contract for the purchase and sale of industrial and mineral products, where the parties have not agreed on a time limit for raising objections to the intrinsic quality of the products and there is no statutory time limit, reference may be made to the provision of Article 15, paragraph 3 of the Regulations on Purchase and Sale Contracts of Industrial and Mineral Products, and the buyer shall raise objections within six months from the date of receipt of the goods. The limitation of action shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Article 136 of the General Principles of the Civil Law.
September 13, 1993
